q: Many transition elements and their compounds act as good catalysts for specific reactions. (2024)
e: Many transition metals and their compounds act as catalysts due to their variable oxidation states and ability to form complexes.

q: The transition elements usually form coloured compounds and ions. (2025)
e: Transition metal compounds are generally coloured due to d-d electron transitions.

q: Although the 4s orbital is the outermost orbital, it is slightly higher in energy than the 3d orbitals. (2025)
e: The 4s orbital is slightly lower in energy than the 3d orbitals when filling.

q: Transition elements are significantly more reactive than Group 1 metals. (2024)
e: Transition elements are much less reactive than the highly reactive Group 1 alkali metals.

q: In general, transition metals do not corrode readily in the solution. (2025)
e: Transition metals can corrode depending on the solution and environmental conditions.

q: Essential electronic configuration of 24Cr is 4s² 3d⁴. (2026)
e: The electronic configuration of chromium (24Cr) is [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵ due to half-filled subshell stability.

q: The general physical and chemical properties of 3d series transition elements are very similar to those of alkali metals. (2024)
e: Transition elements have higher densities, higher melting points, and distinct chemical behaviors compared to alkali metals.

q: The colours of all 3d transition elements are silvery-white. (2025)
e: While pure transition metals are generally silvery-white (except copper), their compounds display various distinct colors.

q: Transition metals and their compounds are often known as everyday metals. (2026)
e: Common metals used in everyday life such as iron, copper, and nickel are transition metals.

q: The transition elements usually lose the electron from the d orbital first. (2025)
e: Transition elements lose electrons from the outermost ns orbital first before losing (n-1)d electrons.

q: The highest oxidation state is +5 for manganese (25Mn). (2024, 2026)
e: Manganese (25Mn) has a maximum oxidation state of +7.

q: The electronic configuration of Ti can be represented using the argon core as [Ar] 4s² 3d². (2025)
e: Titanium (Z = 22) has the ground state electronic configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d².

q: In general, transition metals corrode readily in the atmosphere. (2024)
e: Most transition metals are relatively resistant to atmospheric corrosion.

q: The 3d series transition elements have low melting points and boiling points. (2026)
e: Transition elements have high melting points and boiling points due to strong metallic bonding.

q: The f-block lanthanide and actinide series are called the outer transition elements. (2025)
e: Lanthanides and actinides are known as inner transition elements.

q: In general, transition metals do not corrode readily in the atmosphere. (2024)
e: Transition metals generally resist atmospheric corrosion compared to highly reactive metals.

q: Nickle(II) ion is a poor reducing agent. (2026)
e: The Nickel(II) ion is stable in aqueous solution and acts as a poor reducing agent.

q: Transition elements are silvery-white except for copper, which is bronwnish-red in colour. (2025)
e: Transition metals are typically silvery-white, with copper being a notable exception exhibiting a brownish-red color.

q: The second series (4d) transition elements run from yttrium through cadmium. (2024)
e: The 4d transition series begins at yttrium (Z = 39) and ends at cadmium (Z = 48).

q: In general, the neutral atoms of most of the transition elements have an essential electronic configuration of (n - 1) d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻². (2026)
e: The general valence shell electronic configuration of transition elements is (n - 1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻².

q: One cubic centimeter (1 cm³) cube of iron is eight times heavier than a 1 dm³ cube of sodium. (2024)
e: A 1 dm³ cube of sodium is significantly larger in volume and mass than a 1 cm³ cube of iron.

q: The number of 3d electrons in Fe²⁺ is 5. (2026)
e: As indicated in the reference key.

q: Transition metals are widely used at the industrial level due to their catalytic properties. (2025)
e: Many industrial processes utilize transition metals as catalysts to increase reaction rates.

q: The properties of transition metals are identical. (2026)
e: Transition metals show trends and similarities, but their specific chemical and physical properties are not identical.
